attrs.justification: The non-gas captive fleet, now sized from the register itself: of the 1,105 plants, the fuel-labelled capacity is 769 MW furnace oil (64 plants), 366 MW bagasse (25), 351 MW coal (9), 126 MW biomass (9) and 64 MW diesel (3), against 1,294 MW of gas - so the unestimated fleet is comparable in capacity to the estimated one. What has not been obtained is metered fuel for any of it; the estimated category is natural gas only and its name says so. See captive-nongas-fuels.

attrs.category: Manufacturing industries and construction - all other
attrs.justification: NO LONGER THE GAP IT WAS: the rc46 activation put the measured HDIP coal-by-consumer series INTO the reference - brick-kiln coal 2.78 and cement-sector coal 10.80 Mt through the industrial_solid_fuels_1a2 scope gate - and the supply-consumption identity (imports+production exhausts the consumer columns to ~0.5 kt in 8 of 9 years) closed the old industrial-coal/petcoke refusal: 'other industrial coal' is definitionally ~zero and petcoke rides the Comtrade lane. EDGAR puts Pakistani industrial combustion near 44 Mt CO2e against the engine's 22.58, and the ~15.9 Mt benchmark residual (outputs/industry_fuel_ledger_2024.csv) is now benchmark disagreement over an exhaustive consumer series, bounded but not decomposable: its remaining named claimants are the cement transferred-intensity model's EXCESS over the measured series (+1.2 to +4.9 Mt, configuration cement_kiln_fuel_in_scope) and the process-bagasse ceiling (0.39 Mt). The brick and captive screenings retired at rc47 Wave 0 - superseded_by_reference_stream in the fuel ledger; adding either to a reference that books the measured series would double-count, which is exactly what their configurations briefly did. What would still move this category is a Pakistani kiln heat-intensity audit (to settle the cement excess) and industrial fuel by type beyond the Statistical Supplement's consumer split - HDIP Pakistan Energy Yearbook (paid, eyb@hdip.gov.pk) or OCAC (members-only).

SCREENED, not estimated: the two blockers the earlier row named - a marine factor choice and a domestic/foreign boundary review - are made in sectors/transport/navigation_screen.py, and every held OCAC edition's Domestic Bunkers row is converted in outputs/transport_navigation_screen_2024.csv (3,054 t HSD in the FY2023-24 reference year, 0.0098 Mt CO2e on IPCC Tables 3.5.2/3.5.3). It stays NE for two stated reasons: the reference-year totals are frozen through the release-candidate series, and the ten held editions span 32 to 8,342 t with no trend - an activity that volatile needs the port-side series before it can carry an E. See marine-domestic.

Would be a memo item if it were estimated. NOT to be taken from the 'Overseas/Export' line of OGRA Table 2.1: that line is exported furnace-oil CARGO, not fuel bunkered at Pakistani ports - 1.01 Mt for FY2023-24 against 1.11 Mt of furnace-oil exports reported for calendar 2024. Pakistan had no formal bunkering market until 2026. Recorded so nobody builds the sector on that line.

MATERIAL AND SCREENED, previously undeclared: OGRA's held commercial gas class (45 MMCFD, counted once as post-meter leakage and never as combustion) and the chart-read commercial LPG (~520 kt) screen at roughly 2.4 Mt CO2e between them (outputs/commercial_institutional_audit_2024.csv), below Pakistan's own BUR-1 commercial filing of 3.8 Mt as a two-stream floor should be. Stays NE for stated reasons: the reference-year totals are frozen through the release-candidate series, and the commercial share of retail petroleum is unresolvable within OCAC's held classes without the HDIP commercial energy balance. See commercial-institutional.

Domestic biogas digesters exist in Pakistan (PCRET-supported units, cattle-belt provinces); the programme installation records that would count them have not been obtained here, and HIES carries no biogas consumption item to fall back on. Combustion CO2 would be biogenic; the reportable quantities are digester leakage CH4 and the manure-management transfer, both unestimated. Believed small: electrification and gas/LPG penetration cap the niche. See residential-biogas.

The 8.3 kt of charcoal burned implies roughly 35-50 kt of wood carbonised upstream (4-6 kg wood per kg charcoal), with kiln CH4 that IPCC books to the producing category. No Pakistani charcoal-production statistic exists; the quantity is bounded by the burned charcoal itself and is far below the firewood stream's uncertainty band.

The fuel is IDENTIFIED AND PRICED, the scope is not attributed: the OCAC customer bridge assigns 120,758 t of military/government jet fuel, 4,542 t of 100LL and 12,282 t of unresolved government JP-1 - about 0.435 Mt CO2, priced as memo rows in outputs/aviation_totals_fy2023_24.csv, restated as the observed-unallocated account outputs/aviation_unallocated_fuel_fy2023_24.csv (each tonne with an evidence class, a disposition and a named closer), and as three independent national configurations (military_government_in_scope, general_aviation_in_scope, unresolved_jp1_in_scope; the split of one lumped axis) - but no record attributes the activity between military operations and civil government use, and IPCC reports military aviation under 1A5b. See aviation-1a5b-scope.

Coal mining and handling. PARTIALLY SCREENED: the dominant share of production was held all along - NEPRA Table 21 mine-mouth deliveries to the four Thar plants, 13.24 Mt lignite in FY2023-24 - and the Tier 1 surface band on it is 0.07-0.55 Mt CO2e (outputs/fugitives_coal_screen_2024.csv). The bound is partial by construction and stays NE: underground mining (Balochistan, KP, Punjab) runs thirty times the surface low per tonne, no underground production figure is held, and no Pakistani mine-gas measurement exists. See fugitive-solid-fuels and coal-mine-gas.

attrs.category: Fugitive emissions - gas transmission and distribution
attrs.justification: The largest omission inside 1.B.2 and the cheapest to close: IPCC drives it from utility sales, and OGRA publishes an unaccounted-for-gas line in a free report this inventory already uses for three other numbers.

attrs.category: Fugitive emissions - refining, well drilling, testing and servicing
attrs.justification: Tier 1 wants refinery throughput and well counts; the Year Book carries production only. Small against production.
The 2022 CRT contains lime activity and emissions, but an independent FY2023-24 marketed-plus-captive lime series by type has not been compiled here. See lime-production.

One of two identified plants has production (Fatima Sadiqabad, 563,701 t, calendar 2022) and its ACM0019 abatement history is loaded; the Wave 4 screening prices the unabated and last-verified-abatement readings as configurations, and the category stays NE until matched-year production and operating abatement evidence arrive. This row was MISSING from the register until Wave 4 - the same silent-absence class the 1.A.4.a audit closed - while the sector-level IPPU view carried it at critical materiality. See nitric-acid-production.

attrs.category: Product uses as substitutes for ODS (F-gases)
attrs.justification: The Ozone Secretariat reports a 2024 HFC-consumption control and the species-aware equipment-bank engine is implemented. Chemical/application imports, installed banks, leakage, retirement and recovery are not yet reconciled, so consumption is not treated as annual emissions.

Refrigerant leakage from vehicle air-conditioning is IPPU 2.F.1, not combustion, so it is outside the fuel anchor by construction - but it is a real transport-fleet emission this inventory does not yet report anywhere: the 2.F species-aware bank engine is implemented and the Ozone Secretariat's 2024 consumption control is loaded, but the mobile-air-conditioning application split has not been reconciled here. See transport-mobile-ac-hfc.

attrs.category: Agricultural soils - N from SOC mineralisation (FSOM)
attrs.justification: Set 0 at Tier 1; requires land-use/management-change activity data.

Not estimated: assumed negligible on Pakistan's alkaline/calcareous cropland soils, pending national lime-use activity data (NE rather than NO, since the activity is not demonstrated to be absent). rc39 A4: this NE used to share an engine category with 3.H, which published a 0.000000 Gg liming row - a zero asserts a measurement, so the row was withdrawn and 3.G now maps to no engine category at all. Eq 11.12 and the IPCC Table 11.2 factors are held; only the activity statistic is missing.
Minor; not separately quantified.

Construction and demolition waste is largely inert (near-zero degradable carbon), so its CH4 potential is small by composition - but its tonnage is unquantified and it is a distinct absence from industrial waste, with a different closing source: the Urban Unit's tehsil-level service and facility mapping covers Punjab and has not been obtained. See waste-construction.

The estimated category is municipal solid waste only. Industrial solid waste reaching disposal sites has no national tonnage here; the provincial EPAs' industrial waste returns are the closing source. See waste-industrial.

attrs.category: Biological treatment of solid waste (composting, anaerobic digestion)
attrs.justification: Municipal composting operates at city scale - Lahore's composting facility is the largest, with smaller plants elsewhere - but no national throughput series has been compiled here. Believed small against 4.A, and the omission biases 4.A UP rather than the total down: the streams composting diverts currently sit inside the collected tonnage and decay at the disposal MCF, so estimating 4.B would move emissions out of 4.A, not add them. See waste-biological-treatment.

No municipal-scale incineration operates in Pakistan, but hospital and clinical-waste incinerators do; their throughput has not been obtained here. Bounded far below 4.C.2, whose 3.83 Mt of open burning dwarfs any clinical stream. See waste-incineration.
Needs industrial output by sector and wastewater organic loading, neither of which is available; blocked with 1.A.2 on the same HDIP/industry data.
Cropland-remaining-cropland SOC change set 0 at Tier 1 (matches FAOSTAT).
Grassland SOC change set 0 at Tier 1 (matches FAOSTAT).
Not quantified at Tier 1.
Not quantified; small and outside the agricultural land base.

attrs.category: Air pollutants - road transport cold-start excess
attrs.justification: Excess emissions during engine warm-up are a separate EMEP/EEA process (2023 guidebook ch 1.A.3.b hot/cold methodology) requiring trip counts, trip lengths and ambient temperature on top of the hot-exhaust factors; none of those inputs has been assembled here. The exploratory diagnostic is hot-exhaust-only. See transport-cold-start.

EMEP/EEA 2023 lists NH3 as not estimated for gas, liquid and solid fuel combustion in 1.A.2 and AP-42's combustion chapters carry no NH3 row; the one South Asian kiln measurement (Stockwell et al. 2016: below detection for a zig-zag kiln, 0.429 g/kg fuel for a clamp kiln) is not held. Absent, not zero. See air-industry-nh3.

attrs.category: Air pollutants - flare and refinery species not estimated by the chapters
attrs.justification: EMEP/EEA 2023 1.B.2.c lists NH3 not estimated for flaring; 1.B.2.a.iv lists BC not estimated for refining. Typed absence rows inside the class detail; the fugitives NH3 cell of the coverage matrix is NE on this row. See air-fugitives-species.
The fugitives module carries venting inside its production CH4 factors and holds no vented-volume series; EMEP 1.B.2.c Tier 1 prices flaring only. See air-fugitives-venting.

The EEDB publishes HC (unspeciated exhaust hydrocarbons); the vocabulary rule forbids renaming it NMVOC without a documented methane basis, so the nine-year panel writes aviation NMVOC as NE while the HC series ships as a supplemental species. See air-aviation-nmvoc.

attrs.category: Air pollutants - road transport evaporative NMVOC
attrs.justification: Estimated by the air program's Tier 1 refactor: the 1.A.3.b.v Gasoline evaporation chapter was acquired (sources/EMEP/) and its per-vehicle-day factors (20-35 C band) ride the fleet model's own active petrol counts as separate evaporative atoms in pkinv.sectors.transport.air_pollutants. The year-round hottest-band assumption is the layer's declared limitation. Gap transport-evaporative-nmvoc is CLOSED.

The module's post-meter CH4 carries the leak; an NMVOC term needs the C2+ content of sales gas, which is not held (gas_ch4_fraction 0.90 is CH4 by mass, not an NMVOC fraction). See air-fugitives-composition.

attrs.category: Air pollutants - LNG import terminal and oil pipeline NMVOC
attrs.justification: The EMEP 1.B.2 chapters print no Tier 1 NMVOC factor for regasification terminals; the imported-oil transport factor is held but the module's oil-pipeline anchor is a diagnostic length, not a throughput. See air-fugitives-segments.

attrs.category: Air pollutants - fugitive NMVOC from oil and gas segments
attrs.justification: A PROVISIONAL ESTIMATE since rc59: NMVOC per segment on the fugitives module's own fiscal anchors - gas exploration, production and processing on gross production (EMEP 1.B.2.a.i Table 3-5, one summed factor applied once), transmission and distribution on transmission throughput (1.B.2.b Table 3-6, one summed factor), domestic crude on oil production (1.B.2.a.i Table 3-2, the chapter's 1.16 m3/t), refining and storage on the module's refinery-feed proxy (1.B.2.a.iv Tier 1, the other-regions row: no Stage I or LDAR regime; NOx, CO, SO2 and particulate from refinery process units beside the NMVOC), and petrol depot, delivery and refuelling on OCAC's motor-spirit total (1.B.2.a.v Tier 1 uncontrolled, the chapter's instruction for countries without Stage I/II; vehicle-side evaporation stays in transport's 1.A.3.b.v). UFG is never an activity. Post-meter, venting and LNG terminals are typed absent (below).

attrs.category: Air pollutants - ammonia and soda ash process species not estimated by the chapters
attrs.justification: EMEP/EEA 2023 2.B.1 lists NMVOC, SOx and PM2.5 as not estimated for ammonia production and 2.B.7 lists PM10, PM2.5 and BC as not estimated for soda ash; each is a typed absence row inside the class detail, never a zero. See air-ippu-species.

attrs.category: Air pollutants - nitric acid process NOx
attrs.justification: The EMEP 2.B.2 factor is held; no fiscal nitric-acid production series is (one calendar-2022 point, which cannot back-cast to FY2015-16). See air-ippu-nitric.

A PROVISIONAL ESTIMATE since rc59, inside the covered air panel: ammonia synthesis (NOx, CO, NH3 on EMEP/EEA 2023 2.B.1 Tier 1, the NFDC ammonia tonnes behind the greenhouse-gas ammonia stream), electric-route steel (NOx, CO, NMVOC, SO2, TSP, PM10, PM2.5, BC on the 2.C.1 Tier 2 electric-arc rows, the QIM billets behind the steel stream; the Tier 1 uncontrolled-inclusive rows held beside as the bracket) and Solvay soda ash (CO, NH3, TSP on 2.B.7 Tier 1; the QIM item read by name, the general-industry gas stream a declared geography proxy). Every factor row cites page and digest. What the chapters decline to estimate is typed absent per species (air-ippu-species); urea finishing, nitric acid, lime and glass are typed absent classes with their activity beside them (below).

Estimated as of August 2026, closing the recorded EEA-retrieval blocker: the 2023 Guidebook chapter 1.A.3.c was downloadable from the new-site endpoint exactly as the audit reported (sources/EMEP/). Tier 1 Table 3-1 factors on the same metered fuel that drives the greenhouse-gas layer: 5.9 kt NOx, 0.15 kt PM2.5, BC as the chapter's 0.65 fraction of PM2.5. SO2 is stoichiometric under explicit Pakistani sulfur cases (10 ppm Euro-V to the 1 percent historical ceiling, a 290-fold span) because no operator fuel-quality certificate is published - see rail-diesel-sulfur. The chapter's printed PM confidence intervals do not bracket their central values; the defect is recorded on the factor rows rather than silently repaired.

attrs.category: Air pollutants - residential gas, LPG and kerosene
attrs.justification: Estimated as of August 2026, closing what was recorded as an EEA-retrieval blocker (the 1.A.4 Small Combustion chapter came off the same new-site endpoint as the railway chapter; sources/EMEP/). Tier 1 energy-basis factors on the same fuel energies the greenhouse-gas side burns: +16 kt NOx - the omission that biased NOx low - and under one percent of the biomass PM2.5, as the old NE note predicted. LPG assigned the gaseous-fuel table (noted on its rows); NH3 not applicable per the chapter, omitted rather than zero-filled; the chapter's own filterable-vs-total PM ambiguity quoted on the PM rows.

attrs.category: Air pollutants - cement kilns and quarrying (IPPU)
attrs.justification: Included in the industry layer's integrated kiln class since rc58 (EMEP 2.A.1 Tier 1 per tonne of clinker, typical abatement inherent to clinker production, beside the AP-42 11.6 kiln gases); the register carries an explicit IE pointer (ippu_cement_process_pm -> cement_kiln_integrated) so the one kiln is never priced twice. Gap air-ippu-cement closed.

Estimated as of August 2026, closing what was recorded as an extraction task: each coal rank's own cumulative size distribution - AP-42 Table 1.1-6 for bituminous (6 percent of filterable at or below 2.5 microns, with its 23 percent at 10 microns reproducing the PM-10 factor already carried, the check on the transcription) and Table 1.7-7 for lignite (10 percent at 2.5, 35 at 10, on the tangential basis). About 63 kt uncontrolled - nearly all coal, and roughly doubled by the rank split because lignite's tonnage per TJ doubles the ash-scaled mass - against residential biomass's 461; the gas-only figure of 1 kt that an earlier note warned would mislead is the smallest term. Same uncontrolled-bound caveat as the row above.

Andreae 2019 field factors on the same dry masses that drive the greenhouse-gas side, dung and wood kept apart because they burn differently. 617 kt PM2.5 and 41 kt BC - about twenty-five times road transport's exhaust PM2.5, which is why this layer was built first.

attrs.category: Air pollutants - industrial bagasse process heat
attrs.justification: No mill-level bagasse fuel series is held (the all-cane ceiling is a greenhouse-gas configuration, not an activity); grid-connected bagasse cogeneration stays in the power screening. See air-industry-bagasse.

Per-kilometre factors on the same survival-weighted vehicle-kilometres that distribute the fuel control total. Unlike the greenhouse-gas side this layer does NOT inherit the fuel anchor, so its magnitude rides the fleet model. PROVENANCE FLAW, declared: the g/km factors are Punjab-workbook transcriptions with no primary citation located (emission_factors_gkm.csv has no provenance column), and the layer is exhaust-only - read it as order-of-magnitude.

attrs.category: Air pollutants - oil and gas flaring and venting
attrs.justification: FLARING is a PROVISIONAL ESTIMATE since rc59 (gap air-fugitives-flaring closed): the World Bank flare-register calendar volumes that drive the fugitives CH4/CO2 estimate, blended half-and-half to the fiscal year (declared), at the EMEP/EEA 2023 1.B.2.c Tier 1 factors per tonne of gas burned (density 0.85 kg/m3, the chapter's own note); SO2 at the chapter's 6.4 ppm sulfur assumption because no flare-gas sulfur evidence is held; BC as the chapter's 24 percent of PM2.5 with its own wide range declared. Refinery flaring is priced per m3 of refinery feed (1.B.2.c Table 3-2). VENTING stays NE (below).

attrs.category: Air pollutants - power generation, as actually emitted
attrs.justification: Needs control-device inventory and performance by unit: which plants have precipitators or flue-gas desulphurisation and at what removal efficiency. The five NEPRA Licensees HSE Performance Evaluation Reports were fetched and audited in August 2026: they publish no per-plant equipment or emissions, but their questionnaire scores licensees on air-quality controls and on submitting environmental monitoring reports - so the data exists at NEPRA as unpublished licensee submissions, and the route is a request to its HSE department. Applying a removal rate without it would be inventing the number that matters most, since it spans an order of magnitude between uncontrolled and well-controlled.

attrs.category: Air pollutants - power generation, uncontrolled bound
attrs.justification: AN UNCONTROLLED SCREENING SCENARIO, NOT AN ESTIMATE - AND NOT A MATHEMATICAL MAXIMUM EITHER, because AP-42 defaults are typical uncontrolled rates rather than worst cases (the row is named to say so). AP-42 factors on the sector's own fuel give roughly 399 kt SO2, 183 kt NOx and 664 kt filterable PM UNCONTROLLED - what leaves the furnace. Pakistan's coal units carry precipitators and the newer ones desulphurisation, and no national dataset records which is fitted where or how it performs, so the controlled figure is the row below. The earlier note here said this was blocked on EMEP/EEA factors; re-deriving from AP-42 showed that was the wrong diagnosis - what was missing was never the factors but the FUEL ANALYSIS, which NEPRA does not publish. Sulfur and ash are carried as published ranges with the uncertainty read off them, as the fugitives sector does. SPLIT BY COAL RANK since August 2026: 79 percent of coal energy is Thar lignite on AP-42 Section 1.7's own factors (30S, 6.5A, its own size distribution) and lignite's 11.9 TJ/Gg NCV, the rest imported bituminous on Section 1.1 (38S, 10A) - the rank split RAISED the bound roughly by half, because a tonne of lignite carries half the energy so the sulfur- and ash-scaled factors nearly double per TJ. Grid bagasse cogeneration is estimated from Section 1.8 (PM and NOx; the section publishes no SOx or CO factor). Grid gas NOx blends the boiler and turbine chapters by the plant ledger's heat-rate classification (80 percent turbine), with the 6 percent unresolved share kept on the boiler factor and reported.

attrs.category: Air pollutants - captive self-generation on coal
attrs.justification: The captive register sizes coal-fired captive plants by capacity only and no metered tonne is held; the greenhouse-gas screening prices a bracket outside every total and the air layer types the class absent. See air-industry-captive-solid.

attrs.category: Air pollutants - other-industry coal inside HDIP's cement column
attrs.justification: HDIP labels the column Cement/Other Industry; the clinker-implied kiln-coal band leaves 1.4-6.4 Mt of it outside the kilns in most years, users unidentified, so no equipment or control can be assigned. The tonnage is written in the industry air detail file beside a typed absence. See air-industry-coal-users.

A PROVISIONAL ESTIMATE since rc58, inside the covered air panel: the same metered gas, liquid and coal quantities behind the 1A2 greenhouse-gas estimate, plus the cement engine's clinker and the power module's captive gas (IPCC 1.A.2, reported here), on factors transcribed with page and digest from the now-held chapters (EMEP/EEA 2023 1.A.2, 2.A.1 and 1.A.4; AP-42 1.3, 1.4, 3.1-3.4, 11.3, 11.6; the World Bank 2020 South Asian kiln field factors). Source-class typical controls: cement kilns carry the particulate collection inherent to clinker production, boilers, engines and brick kilns are uncontrolled. SO2 is a sulfur balance on DATED evidence (HSFO grade mix, the diesel regime, Punjab coalfield ranges) - never the power sector's Thar range. What stays NE is typed by name with its activity beside it: NH3 for every fuel (EMEP lists it not estimated), other-industry coal inside HDIP's cement column, captive solids, industrial bagasse. Equipment shares (boilers/furnaces/engines; engines/boilers for diesel; engines/turbines for captive) are DECLARED and carry 40-50 percent - see air-industry-equipment-mix. The brick kilns carry most of the layer's SO2 and particulate; the integrated cement kiln most of its NOx and CO (the figures are in outputs/pakemis_air_source_class_uncertainty_by_year.csv, per sector, period and species).

attrs.category: Air pollutants - railway non-exhaust PM (wheel, rail and brake wear)
attrs.justification: EXPLORATORY, estimated as of August 2026 and never summed with the EMEP exhaust layer: TNO's fuel-based wear factors (Dutch national inventory update 2024, anchored on an Austrian tonne-km measurement) on the same metered diesel - 20 t TSP, 15 t PM10, 4 t PM2.5 at +/-150 percent, roughly a tenth of exhaust PM10 alongside it. The TNO report's own PM2.5 bullet contradicts its stated size fractions; the factor rows record the discrepancy and adopt the fraction-consistent reading. No Pakistani wear measurement exists; tread brakes and track condition plausibly push the true figure higher, which the declared uncertainty covers. See pkinv.sectors.railways.wear_pm.

attrs.category: Air pollutants - glass furnace process particulate
attrs.justification: The EMEP 2.A.3 chapter is held; the QIM glass item is an area (square metres of sheet) that cannot be priced per tonne without a conversion nobody publishes. See air-ippu-glass.

attrs.category: Air pollutants - road transport non-exhaust PM (tyre, brake and road wear)
attrs.justification: Estimated by the air program's Tier 1 refactor: the 1.A.3.b.vi-vii chapters were acquired (sources/EMEP/) and their g/vkm factors ride the same survival-weighted vehicle-kilometres the fuel split rides, as separate tyre_brake_wear and road_wear atoms - the coarser TSP/PM10 strata beside, never summed into, the PM2.5 core. Road-dust resuspension stays out. Gap transport-nonexhaust-pm is CLOSED.

attrs.category: Air pollutants - lime kiln process particulate
attrs.justification: The EMEP 2.A.2 chapter is held; no lime production series is (PBS QIM lists no lime item; lime CO2 is NE in the greenhouse-gas panel for the same reason). See air-ippu-lime.

attrs.category: Air pollutants - urea prilling and granulation particulate and ammonia
attrs.justification: The EMEP 2.B.10.a row is a sector-wide E-PRTR/Eurostat ratio, inadmissible for a prilling tower (it would print 330 kt of TSP from 6.6 Mt of urea); AP-42 8.2 is the applicable chapter and every epa.gov address tried returned 403. The urea tonnage is written beside the typed absence. See air-ippu-urea.

28% of cattle and 30% of buffalo excreted N burned as household fuel; N removed from Manure Management and RECEIVED BY 1.A.4.b below (pkinv.sectors.residential), which converts it to volatile solids through IPCC Table 10A VS rates for the same animal categories. Closed in both directions and tested with exact equality.

Estimated as of August 2026 from NEPRA SoIR 2024 Table 8's E3 block: eight plants, 726.85 GWh in FY2023-24, reconciled against the table's printed total. CH4 and N2O only, about 0.02 Mt at IPCC Table 2.2 biomass factors (the energy-industries table - the residential one is ten times higher on CH4); biogenic CO2 (about 1.1 Mt) is the sector's memo item. The activity is generation x an assumed 15,000 kJ/kWh heat rate, the sector's one generation-derived stream, and the parameter's note says so. Co-firing is named, not split: three plants list Biomass and one lists furnace oil as alternate fuel, with no published share.

Fuel-based from NEPRA State of Industry Report Table 3, run through IPCC Vol 2 Ch 2 Table 2.2 (Energy Industries) - not the residential Table 2.5. Coal is carried as a bituminous/lignite sensitivity because Thar lignite and imported bituminous are reported together. The sector's one-sided questions - the coal calorific conversion (worth 19.4 Mt), the TOE gross/net basis (5-10% on CO2), K-Electric coverage (a trending 7.1-4.0 Mt) - are named structural cases with conditional intervals in outputs/power_uncertainty_scenarios_fy2023_24.csv, deliberately outside the parametric +/-10.9%, so no probability band conceals them.

The first estimated part of 1.A.2, and measured rather than proxied: OGRA publishes the gas delivered to captive power annually, and a 1,105-plant register built from the SNGPL and SSGC captive fleets and the NEPRA licence list reconciles against it to within 0.01 MMCFD. FY2024, Table 2.3 factors. The dominant uncertainty is the gas heating value, which no Pakistani source pins: 900 against 1,000 Btu/scf moves the category from 4.99 to 5.55 Mt and both are reported.

attrs.category: Captive self-generation - furnace oil / diesel / coal / bagasse
attrs.justification: The non-gas captive fleet, now sized from the register itself: of the 1,105 plants, the fuel-labelled capacity is 769 MW furnace oil (64 plants), 366 MW bagasse (25), 351 MW coal (9), 126 MW biomass (9) and 64 MW diesel (3), against 1,294 MW of gas - so the unestimated fleet is comparable in capacity to the estimated one. What has not been obtained is metered fuel for any of it; the estimated category is natural gas only and its name says so. See captive-nongas-fuels.

Industrial self-generation liquids are IPCC 1.A.2 and are INCLUDED ELSEWHERE in two places. Bulk purchases (the channel a captive plant of any size buys through) sit inside the ESTIMATED 1.A.2 industrial liquids - OCAC's Total Industry customer-class rows (src/pkinv/sectors/industry/data.py), which the transport fuel ledger excludes from the road control by construction (its RESOLVED-OBSERVED Industry claimant row). Only retail-pump captive diesel remains inside the 1.A.3.b Road control at road factors - the UNRESOLVED claimant row 'Captive generation (retail)' of outputs/transport_fuel_ledger_2024.csv, declared as biasing road transport high. Captive GAS self-generation is a separate, estimated category (computed by the power module, reported under industry through data/stream_reporting_sector.csv); this row is its liquid-fuel sibling. See transport-hsd-end-use.

IPCC books construction and industrial off-road machinery under 1.A.2 (gvii), NOT under 1.A.4.c - a mapping this inventory previously overgeneralised. The fuel is reported inside the Mixed off-road (1A4c/1A2) category, whose class is the source workbook's residual bucket as well as its tractor class, so whatever construction plant the residual contains is estimated there at Table 3.3.1 factors and allocated on a cropland proxy that is wrong for it. Splitting the residual needs equipment stock data no source here provides.

The second estimated part of 1.A.2 and the largest of the three: OGRA's sector-wise gas table reports 291 MMCFD to General Industry and 0.1 to cement, metered by the utilities. Table 2.3 factors, the industrial ones - Table 2.5's residential CH4 is five times higher. PROCESS HEAT, BOILERS AND KILNS, not self-generation, which is the separate captive row above. The fertiliser row of the same table, 756 MMCFD and the second largest in the country, is deliberately EXCLUDED on the IPCC ammonia method: the plant's total gas requirement - feedstock and process fuel together, 83.5/16.5 on NFDC's monthly plant annex for this very fiscal year - belongs to 2.B.1, and only separately metered auxiliary combustion outside the process boundary would stay here. The feedstock carbon leaves as urea and is priced by the 2.B.1 ledger and at application in 3.H. NFDC's monthly plant annex puts THIS fiscal year at 83.5/16.5 and its 751.9 MMCFD agrees with OGRA's 756 to half a percent, two independent records of the same year.

attrs.category: Manufacturing industries and construction - all other
attrs.justification: NO LONGER THE GAP IT WAS: the rc46 activation put the measured HDIP coal-by-consumer series INTO the reference - brick-kiln coal 2.78 and cement-sector coal 10.80 Mt through the industrial_solid_fuels_1a2 scope gate - and the supply-consumption identity (imports+production exhausts the consumer columns to ~0.5 kt in 8 of 9 years) closed the old industrial-coal/petcoke refusal: 'other industrial coal' is definitionally ~zero and petcoke rides the Comtrade lane. EDGAR puts Pakistani industrial combustion near 44 Mt CO2e against the engine's 22.58, and the ~15.9 Mt benchmark residual (outputs/industry_fuel_ledger_2024.csv) is now benchmark disagreement over an exhaustive consumer series, bounded but not decomposable: its remaining named claimants are the cement transferred-intensity model's EXCESS over the measured series (+1.2 to +4.9 Mt, configuration cement_kiln_fuel_in_scope) and the process-bagasse ceiling (0.39 Mt). The brick and captive screenings retired at rc47 Wave 0 - superseded_by_reference_stream in the fuel ledger; adding either to a reference that books the measured series would double-count, which is exactly what their configurations briefly did. What would still move this category is a Pakistani kiln heat-intensity audit (to settle the cement excess) and industrial fuel by type beyond the Statistical Supplement's consumer split - HDIP Pakistan Energy Yearbook (paid, eyb@hdip.gov.pk) or OCAC (members-only).

The third estimated part of 1.A.2, and the one that was here all along: OCAC's Total Industry customer class reports 642,021 t furnace oil, 400,400 t diesel, 24,697 t gasoline, 6,973 t kerosene, 1,670 t LDO and 959 t HOBC for FY2023-24 - 3.40 Mt CO2e on Table 2.3 factors and Table 1.2 net calorific values. Those rows sit in the same annual OCAC panel the transport sector has ingested since its first release; nothing read them, and the gap register called the fuel not-acquired while the tonnages were committed to the repository. LDO has no IPCC line of its own and takes the Gas/Diesel Oil factor with a widened calorific uncertainty. The same publication's monthly editions give the whole sector its seasonal profile - see pkinv.sectors.industry.monthly.

attrs.category: Railways - non-traction fuel (workshops, power houses, pumps, track machinery)
attrs.justification: MEASURED AND, SINCE the rail re-base, BOOKED AT ITS OWN CATEGORY rather than declared IE inside 1.A.3.c: 1,599 thousand litres of diesel (1.21 percent of the account) plus most of the furnace-oil stream, via the Year Book detail table read by pkinv.sectors.railways.reconcile. By IPCC definition track machinery is off-road transport, workshops and power houses are stationary combustion, and pumps follow their end use - and the source publishes no split below the one non-locomotive figure, which is why the category name says unresolved instead of picking a single destination. Rail factors are retained (no use-specific factor is supportable), so the re-base conserves the module and national totals exactly; the pre-older declared-IE booking survives as the rail_ie_summary configuration. Spatially the category sits at the seven divisional yards (S2), not along the line - the reason the railways module is no longer wholly S1.

LTO cycles from CAA movement statistics x ICAO fuel-burn tables, full-flight for domestic. International bunkers are a memo item ESTIMATED at full flight by the source-row-conserving JP-1 bridge (550,670 t of commercial JP-1, 1.740 Mt CO2, outputs/aviation_bridge_2024.csv); the 210.4 kt international-LTO figure is a separate local-air product, not the bunkers estimate.

Zero direct combustion by definition, and the registered electric fleet is negligible in the 2022 registration data. Electricity-related emissions are counted at the power station in 1.A.1.a like all consumption - the Orange Line convention. Recorded so the road scope statement has a boundary row rather than an implicit omission.

ANCHORED ON FUEL, not on the fleet model: the OCAC FY2023-24 Road customer-class rows (petrol MS+HOBC and HSD - bulk industry, power, government and railway diesel excluded by the source's own partition), net of the household-generator petrol carve-out relayed from the residential sector, plus CNG from OGRA's metered sector gas on its own activity basis. The railway figure is an independent cross-check (Year Book FY2023-24 row vs OCAC Railways row, 3.8 percent apart), not a deduction. outputs/transport_fuel_ledger_2024.csv is the executable two-tier claimant structure. KNOWN FLAW: the class split rides vehicle-kilometres, over-weighting motorcycles; the total is unaffected because it is set by the fuel rows. Retail-bought agricultural-stationary, captive and other non-road diesel remains inside the Road row (the ledger's UNRESOLVED rows), biasing 1.A.3.b high conditional on the other deductions; the retail_nonroad scenarios price the claim.

LOCOMOTIVE TRACTION ONLY under the re-based reference (0.38939 Mt): the Year Book detail table splits locomotive from other-than-locomotive fuel, and the measured non-traction share books at its own category row below. Pakistan Railways Year Book metered fuel consumption x IPCC Vol 2 Ch 3 Table 3.4.1, the RAIL table - its N2O factor is seven times the road value. Railway diesel is its own OCAC customer-class row, outside the road control by the source's structure, and the Year Book figure serves as an independent cross-check on that row (3.8 percent apart at the matched year) rather than a deduction. The mainline network has been diesel-only since about 2010 (electric energy NIL from the 2010-2015 quinquennium in the Year Book's own historical table), so there is no scope-2 stream in the inventory years; urban electric rail (Lahore Orange Line) is outside the operator, has zero direct 1A3c combustion, and its electricity is accounted under power. Matched-year check: BUR-1 reports 4.06 Mt for FY2017-18 against 0.466 Mt here by the identical method on the same year's fuel; see the module docstring for the fuel and train-kilometre arithmetic.

Zero direct combustion by definition: the Orange Line is an electric metro outside Pakistan Railways, and its electricity-related emissions are counted at the power station in 1.A.1.a like all consumption. Recorded so the railway scope statement - PR mainline direct combustion - has a boundary row rather than an implicit omission.

SCREENED, not estimated: the two blockers the earlier row named - a marine factor choice and a domestic/foreign boundary review - are made in sectors/transport/navigation_screen.py, and every held OCAC edition's Domestic Bunkers row is converted in outputs/transport_navigation_screen_2024.csv (3,054 t HSD in the FY2023-24 reference year, 0.0098 Mt CO2e on IPCC Tables 3.5.2/3.5.3). It stays NE for two stated reasons: the reference-year totals are frozen through the release-candidate series, and the ten held editions span 32 to 8,342 t with no trend - an activity that volatile needs the port-side series before it can carry an E. See marine-domestic.

Would be a memo item if it were estimated. NOT to be taken from the 'Overseas/Export' line of OGRA Table 2.1: that line is exported furnace-oil CARGO, not fuel bunkered at Pakistani ports - 1.01 Mt for FY2023-24 against 1.11 Mt of furnace-oil exports reported for calendar 2024. Pakistan had no formal bunkering market until 2026. Recorded so nobody builds the sector on that line.

MATERIAL AND SCREENED, previously undeclared: OGRA's held commercial gas class (45 MMCFD, counted once as post-meter leakage and never as combustion) and the chart-read commercial LPG (~520 kt) screen at roughly 2.4 Mt CO2e between them (outputs/commercial_institutional_audit_2024.csv), below Pakistan's own BUR-1 commercial filing of 3.8 Mt as a two-stream floor should be. Stays NE for stated reasons: the reference-year totals are frozen through the release-candidate series, and the commercial share of retail petroleum is unresolvable within OCAC's held classes without the HDIP commercial energy balance. See commercial-institutional.
Household electricity is nearly half of national consumption and is counted at the point of generation in 1.A.1.a. Deliberately absent; a test asserts no electricity stream exists.

Domestic biogas digesters exist in Pakistan (PCRET-supported units, cattle-belt provinces); the programme installation records that would count them have not been obtained here, and HIES carries no biogas consumption item to fall back on. Combustion CO2 would be biogenic; the reportable quantities are digester leakage CH4 and the manure-management transfer, both unestimated. Believed small: electrification and gas/LPG penetration cap the niche. See residential-biogas.

attrs.category: Residential - crop residues and cotton sticks
attrs.justification: An upper-bound residential allocation of the agriculture residue ledger's fuel destination: frac_fuel covers all fuel use (R_fuel = R_household + R_commercial/industrial + R_unresolved), and the whole 9.3 Mt dry (10.5 Mt air-dry) is booked here, which can only overstate households. The ledger closes returned+burned+fuel+other==1 per crop, so this stream cannot overlap field burning or the soils return; HIES prices bracket the mass (7.8-24.7 Mt air-dry, the ledger's 10.5 inside) and the expenditure items - residue fuel in 16.5% and 7.1% of households - are the future constraint on the household share.
Receives the IE transfer above. Biogenic CO2 is reported as a memo item.

HIES 2024-25 design-weighted household quantity: 23.1 Mt air-dry wood, a measurement replacing FAOSTAT's flagged, unmoving estimate. Twice corroborated - HIES 2018-19 agrees within 6%, FAOSTAT's moisture-matched equivalent within 7% - and carried at 35% activity uncertainty (down from 60) with the FAOSTAT path retained as a structural scenario. See firewood-quantity in data/data_gaps.csv (closed) and outputs/residential_hies_comparison_2024.csv.

attrs.category: Residential - biogenic CO2 (dung cake, firewood, residues, charcoal)
attrs.justification: Memo item, outside the national total, per IPCC's biomass convention and Pakistan's own BUR-1. Any net stock loss belongs in LULUCF.

The 8.3 kt of charcoal burned implies roughly 35-50 kt of wood carbonised upstream (4-6 kg wood per kg charcoal), with kiln CH4 that IPCC books to the producing category. No Pakistani charcoal-production statistic exists; the quantity is bounded by the burned charcoal itself and is far below the firewood stream's uncertainty band.

HIES 2024-25 design-weighted quantities - 13.2 kt coal, 8.3 kt charcoal, each on about one household in a thousand, three orders below firewood. OGRA's nil household coal row was roughly right for the wrong reason (a quantity too small for a supply table to resolve, not an absent market). Coal CO2 counted; charcoal CO2 is a biogenic memo. See residential-coal-charcoal (closed).
OGRA national supply x a domestic share read from OGRA Figure 5.2, which is published only as a bar chart.
OCAC total SKO, treated in full as household use; an upper bound, but under 0.2 Mt CO2e either way.

HIES 2024-25 generator-fuel expenditure over the administered petrol price: 56 kt of petrol, 2,495 TJ, 0.17 Mt CO2e. Carved out of the road-transport petrol control through the same relayed-accessor idiom as railway diesel, asserted with equality - the second deduction on that control. Air-pollutant rows are NOT published for this stream: the EMEP small-combustion chapter has no household-genset class, and road exhaust factors would cross the mobile/stationary boundary. Declared omission, bounded by the 56 kt.

**Defining Vehicle Categories**

I've been working on defining vehicle categories and have added "Electric road vehicles" to the completeness list. The justification is straightforward: these vehicles have zero direct combustion, aligning with the definition, plus the 2022 registration data on EVs shows very low numbers. Electricity-related emissions are accounted for at the power station level.

**Investigating Emission Data Gaps**

I'm digging into the nitric acid production data and noticed a discrepancy. While air pollutants are documented, the GHG side appears missing from the initial data. I'm querying `get_completeness` to confirm the 'Not Estimated' (NE) status and understand why. My approach involves filtering by IPCC code 2B2 and using a specific `ipcc_code` filter, if necessary. I'll need to figure out how to best deal with the NE entries.

One of two identified plants has production (Fatima Sadiqabad, 563,701 t, calendar 2022) and its ACM0019 abatement history is loaded; the Wave 4 screening prices the unabated and last-verified-abatement readings as configurations, and the category stays NE until matched-year production and operating abatement evidence arrive. This row was MISSING from the register until Wave 4 - the same silent-absence class the 1.A.4.a audit closed - while the sector-level IPPU view carried it at critical materiality. D34.text:
**Analyzing the "NO" Reports**

I've determined that "Not Occurring" reports aren't all the same. The electric vehicle case is clear: direct combustion is zero, and the fleet is tiny, with the electricity emissions accounted for elsewhere. So, "NO" there is fundamentally different. It's a key distinction I need to factor into the assessment of similar reports.

No, the inventory reports them as empty for different reasons. 

**Electric road vehicles** are recorded as "Not Occurring" (NO). By definition, electric vehicles have zero direct combustion. The electricity they consume is already counted at the point of generation (power stations), so assigning emissions to the road transport sector would double-count them. The inventory includes the category simply to show that the boundary is closed, rather than implicitly left out. 

**Nitric acid production**, on the other hand, is recorded as "Not Estimated" (NE) because the data needed to price it is missing. While the project holds some historical abatement records for one of the country's two identified plants, it lacks matched-year production volumes and operating abatement evidence across the fiscal years. Without the actual production series, the emissions cannot be reliably estimated.
